run.question:
The checkout-service in production-eu-west-2 is throwing 500s. Please look at
app-264-prod-logs and find the root cause.

report.summary: First and decisive finding: there is no `production-eu-west-2` data behind the index named in the question. `app-264-prod-logs` is the only log index present, and every document in it carries cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2 — including the two checkout-service ERROR lines (total 3 documents, 2 checkout-service + 1 payment-service, in the authorized window 2026-11-21T08:58:52Z–2026-11-22T08:58:52Z). So the index does hold checkout 500 evidence, but it is staging-eu-west-2 evidence, and I do not treat it as the cause of a production-eu-west-2 incident. The 500 line it holds is `POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired` (staging, 2026-11-22T07:58:43Z), accompanied by `Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress` (staging, 06:58:43Z) and a payment-service WARN `Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)` (08:28:43Z) — all staging-labeled test-fixture context, not production telemetry. My Kubernetes access is the staging-eu-west-2 cluster only (7 namespaces, no production namespace; the checkout workload is Deployment checkout in namespace otel-demo), and its checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n was Running and in the sampled window logged successful payments and order confirmations, not 500s. Metrics (Prometheus) and traces (Jaeger) were unreachable on every call (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error rate, latency or trace evidence for any cluster could be obtained, and the production-eu-west-2 500s remain unexplained. Root cause is therefore not named.

claims.text: `app-264-prod-logs` is the only index visible in the log store (health green, 3 documents, 7.7kb); no other log index exists to search for production-eu-west-2.

Aggregated over the whole authorized window (2026-11-21T08:58:52Z–2026-11-22T08:58:52Z), all 3 documents in `app-264-prod-logs` have cluster=staging-eu-west-2 (3/3) and environment=staging (3/3); by service checkout-service=2 and payment-service=1, by level ERROR=2 and WARN=1. There is no bucket for production-eu-west-2 or environment=production in that result.

The three documents in `app-264-prod-logs`, in timestamp order: 2026-11-22T06:58:43Z service=checkout-service level=ERROR "Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress"; 2026-11-22T07:58:43Z service=checkout-service level=ERROR "POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired"; 2026-11-22T08:28:43Z service=payment-service level=WARN "Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)". Each carries cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2.

Restricting the same index to its last hour (2026-11-22T07:58:52Z–2026-11-22T08:58:52Z) returned exactly one document: the payment-service WARN at 2026-11-22T08:28:43Z (cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging). The two checkout-service ERROR lines fall outside that one-hour slice.

Rejected: that `app-264-prod-logs` supplies evidence about checkout 500s in production-eu-west-2. Every document in it is labeled cluster=staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging, region=eu-west-2 (3/3), so its checkout 500 line is staging evidence and cannot be attributed to the production-eu-west-2 incident.

The reachable Kubernetes cluster (staging-eu-west-2) has 7 namespaces — default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo — and no production namespace; all application deployments (including checkout, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, 1/1 ready) run in namespace otel-demo.

Pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (namespace otel-demo, staging-eu-west-2) is Running with restartCount=2, last termination reason "Unknown", started 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z; it is not a pod created inside the incident window.

In the staging-eu-west-2 checkout pod's own logs for 2026-11-22T07:58:52Z–08:58:52Z, the four lines returned by an error/fail/500/stripe filter are all severity=info — "payment went through (transaction_id: e4c4a97a-…)" at 08:33:59Z, again at 08:42:04Z, "order confirmation email sent…" at 08:23:54Z and "[PlaceOrder] user_id=…" at 08:46:23Z; none reports a 500 or a stripe failure. 256 other lines were removed by the filter and remain unknown, and this says nothing about the production-eu-west-2 checkout workload.

Kubernetes events in the authorized window (source_start_at 2026-11-21T09:05:28Z, source_end_at 2026-11-22T08:05:10Z) contain a burst at 2026-11-22T08:04:18Z–08:05:10Z in staging-eu-west-2: SandboxChanged on all 22 otel-demo pods (checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n included at 08:04:18Z, followed by Created/Started at 08:04:19–08:04:20Z), plus Unhealthy liveness/readiness probe failures and BackOff on prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (unhealthy x1 liveness, x6 readiness, BackOff x4 at 08:04:44Z, "Container nginx…") and probe failures on kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz. No checkout 500 or application error event appears.

If the production-eu-west-2 checkout 500s have a payment-credential cause, an expired payment-provider key would be a candidate; the only message naming a checkout 500 in the observed data attributes it to an expired stripe test key used by an integration-test fixture, and it is staging-labeled, so this is unverified for production and is not evidence of the production fault.

Unverified: the repeated metric/trace failures (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every Prometheus and Jaeger call in this Run) may relate to the staging-eu-west-2 prometheus-readonly-proxy crash-loop seen in events (readiness probe connection refused x6, BackOff x4, restarts=6, last state Error); whether these tools query through that proxy is not shown by the evidence, and the pod's current phase is Running.

Point the investigation at real production-eu-west-2 telemetry: have an operator confirm that production log shipping is enabled into an index whose documents carry cluster=production-eu-west-2, and restore the metric and trace backends (Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on get_all_labels, get_label_values, get_metric_names, get_metric_metadata, list_prometheus_rules and execute_prometheus_instant_query; Jaeger on traces_list_services, traces_search and traces_list_operations) so the checkout error rate and trace-level dependency failures can be measured.

gaps: No production-eu-west-2 telemetry exists in the queryable data: the only log index `app-264-prod-logs` holds 3 documents, all labeled cluster=staging-eu-west-2 / environment=staging, so the production-eu-west-2 checkout 500s could not be observed at all.

Prometheus was unavailable for the whole Run: get_all_labels, get_label_values (cluster), get_metric_names, get_metric_metadata, list_prometheus_rules and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency-baseline or kube-state-metrics evidence for any cluster was obtained and no alert rules or firing alerts could be inspected.

Jaeger was unavailable for the whole Run: traces_list_services, traces_search(service=checkout) and traces_list_operations(service=checkout) all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout's spans, error statuses, parent-child call edges and dependency attribution are unknown.

A service name `checkout-service` is used in the log store's service field while the reachable Kubernetes workload is Deployment `checkout` in namespace `otel-demo` (staging-eu-west-2); no Kubernetes object named checkout-service was observed, and no production Kubernetes cluster is readable to check the production naming.
The previous container instance of checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n had 0 log lines available, so the cause of its earlier restarts (restartCount=2, last termination reason "Unknown") is unknown.

change_history is not integrated, so deploys, config changes and rollbacks — including the "deploy-v2.3.4 rollback" text seen only in staging logs — cannot be confirmed as events in production-eu-west-2.
No Secrets are readable, so any payment-provider credential value (e.g. a stripe key) in any environment could not be verified.

Whether the staging-eu-west-2 checkout 500s at 06:58:43Z and 07:58:43Z affected real staging traffic is unknown: the 256 filtered-out log lines were not read and no metric or trace source was available to measure them.
next_steps: Confirm with the platform owner whether production-eu-west-2 logs are shipped anywhere; the index named in the question currently receives only staging-eu-west-2, environment=staging documents.

Once production log/metric/trace access is available, compare checkout's 5xx rate and latency against a pre-incident baseline and inspect failing checkout spans for the dependency that returns the error, rather than assuming the staging stripe-fixture message applies.

In staging-eu-west-2, have an operator inspect prometheus-readonly-proxy (namespace otel-demo) restart cause and config, since it was crash-looping around 2026-11-22T08:04-08:05Z, to restore metric visibility.

Ask the owning team to review the payment provider credential/configuration used by checkout in the affected environment, and treat the staging "integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired" line as a staging test-fixture issue until production evidence confirms otherwise.
